note: Balanced curated accounts; leans describe the account, not each post. Midterms 2026 post-election window.

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: A lot of "fundamentals" type election models implicitly assume that parties respond fairly rationally to incentives. I'm not sure you can really say Trump is doing that when they lose an election by 13+ points and then elevate Hegseth and Stephen Miller.

posts.name: Byron York
posts.text: Reading through Thomas Massie's articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. There are 8 articles. Articles 1, 2, and 3 all accuse Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution by waging war in Iran.

posts.name: CNN Politics
posts.text: In a Senate race that is still too close to call, Mississippi state election officials are facing intense scrutiny over their methods for maintaining voter rolls after thousands of voters cast provisional ballots...

posts.name: Aaron Rupar
posts.text: Even Hassett can't spin hotter than expected inflation data: "It's a disappointing report ... things have accelerated over the last three months ... the trickle down from higher energy prices is definitely very palpable in the data"

posts.name: Kyle Kondik
posts.text: I thought if the Dems won the Senate, the Iran war would be the main reason why (because of its depressing effect on Trump's approval, particularly in states he won by double digits). But given the size of the drubbing maybe the Senate would've flipped anyway.

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: We are one week removed from the election. Republicans contend a failed war in Iran was the reason for the loss. They have still fired no one. The RNC Chair remains as well.

posts.name: POLITICO
posts.text: House GOP leaders face their post-election reckoning

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text: In California's 22nd House district, incumbent Republican David Valadao is trailing by a 36-point margin, one of the worst totals of any incumbent member of Congress in recent American history. This majority-Hispanic district would have backed Trump by two points in 2024.

posts.name: Matthew Yglesias
posts.text: Not questioning Hinojosa's political judgment, she obviously did great. I just think "the optimal top state income tax rate is zero" as a policy idea is a little disappointing on the merits.

posts.name: Byron York
posts.text: Trump yields on immigration enforcement. For the first time since taking office in January 2025, Trump sent a strong message to some illegal immigrants that they will be allowed to stay in the US. That was a stunning change in direction on the administration's signature issue.

posts.name: Punchbowl News
posts.text: For tech and artificial intelligence, the biggest institutional changes on the Hill next year may come from the House and Senate Judiciary Committees. Here's what to look for on panels with oversight of antitrust, intellectual property and more.

posts.name: G Elliott Morris
posts.text: Given the effect size of extra ads, Democrats arguably could have won back the Senate with a ~25-35% reduction in spending. (Don't tell the consultants)

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: 65,386 Georgians showed up to vote in 2026 and refused to vote in the Senate race. 33,256 refused to vote in the gubernatorial race. Even had they all voted in each race, the Republicans would not have won.

posts.name: G Elliott Morris
posts.text: Incorporating 2026 results, the cycle-to-cycle correlation in polling error since 1990 (signed error) is now -0.14. Before 2026, it was -0.04. There is no relationship between lagged cycle polling error and error in the next cycle.

posts.name: Dave Wasserman
posts.text: With Dems all but certain to prevail in Mississippi and Alaska, we're most likely looking at a 56D-44R Senate and a ~260D-175R House, which would be Dems' largest House majority since 1992.

Last night was the largest blue wave in a generation.

Democrats have been projected as winner in 54 Senate seats, flipping seven states and with a lead in two others (Alaska and Mississippi).

In the House, Democrats have been projected in 249 seats - a net gain of 38 so far.
